title: SCAT Airlines 760

location.name: Kyzyltu, 1.6 km short of Almaty runway 23R

summary: SCAT Airlines Flight 760 crashed on 29 January 2013 during go-around to Almaty. At 07:03:24 UTC, the CRJ200 was at 1,600 m altitude on final approach in thick freezing fog with runway visibility of 175-200 m when the crew initiated a go-around due to inability to see the runway. Fourteen seconds after initiating the go-around, the aircraft entered an uncontrolled nose-down dive at approximately 20 degrees pitch-down. The aircraft impacted the ground 1.6 km short of the runway near Kyzyltu, killing all 21 occupants.
probable_cause: The nose-down elevator deflection during go-around maneuvering was the result of pilot input, though the investigation could not determine why the pilot made these control inputs (p. 3278-3315). Possible scenarios included: spatial disorientation from instrument meteorological conditions and turbulence; pilot incapacitation from sudden medical event (autopsy revealed Captain had coronary artery disease with significant stenosis); or somatogravitational illusion causing inversion of pilot's pitch perception during dynamic flight in poor visibility (p. 2048-2050, 3300-3315).

factors.evidence: Approach in freezing fog with runway visibility 175-200 m, below operator's meteorological minimums for crew's CAT I certification (p. 2362-2368)
Go-around initiated at 07:03:24 UTC when visibility remained below operating minimums (p. 2367-2369)
Autopsy revealed Captain Evdokimov had coronary artery disease with significant stenosis; sudden medical incapacitation scenario would cause uncontrolled input to control yoke (p. 3300-3310)
Aircraft descended from 1,600 m in uncontrolled dive with pitch 20-25 degrees nose-down, speed 360+ kt, impacting ground 1.6 km short of runway at 07:03:38 UTC, killing all occupants (p. 1675, 3278)

events.text: Takeoff from Kokshetau airport; Captain monitoring, Second Officer flying; automatic climb mode (p. 2236)
Reached cruise altitude 10,650 m, cruise speed 460 km/h in automatic mode (p. 2236)
Captain took control; Second Officer moved to radio duties without formal handover (p. 2236)
Captain reported: ETA 06:55, weather min CAT II 30x300, alternates Chymkent/Karaganda, fuel 2.5 hrs (p. 2236)
Descent initiated, aircraft 160 km from Almaty (p. 2236)
At 7,000 m, 540 km/h: Captain commanded 'Cowl on' - engine anti-ice system activated (p. 2236)
Approach clearance obtained, descending toward Almaty with visibility 175 m reported (p. 2237)
Captain confirmed decision to descend to runway visual range (VPR) despite below-minimums visibility (p. 2237)
Aircraft level at 1,600 m altitude in automatic mode - altitude hold active, navigation mode in lateral channel (p. 2237)
Flaps extended to 8 degrees during right turn to heading 230; aircraft positioning for landing approach (p. 2237)
ATIS Sierra: visibility improved to 300 m midpoint. Captain satisfied: 'OK, 3 hundred, that's fine, we need the start' (p. 2238)
Flaps to 8 degrees during turn to heading 140; speed 345 km/h at 1,600 m altitude (p. 2238)
Go-around initiated: runway not visible at descent minimum altitude, visual contact lost (p. 3278)
Fourteen seconds into go-around: elevator deflection commanded uncontrolled nose-down dive, pitch changed to -20 degrees (p. 3278, 2048-2050)
Aircraft crashed 1.6 km short of runway 23R near Kyzyltu at pitch 20 degrees nose-down, 360+ kt speed, landing gear down, flaps 10-15 degrees. All 21 killed (p. 1675, 3278)

recommendations.text: Establish standardized procedures ensuring crew compliance with meteorological minimums and decision-making protocols during approaches below certification limits

notes: 15 detailed events with UTC clock times extracted from Russian MAK report
Root cause undetermined; elevator deflection confirmed as pilot input via mathematical modeling
Possible factors: spatial disorientation, medical incapacitation, somatogravitational illusion
